# First race track: layout options (RACE-002)

## Decision (owner, 2026-10-17)

> "i love all the mechanics except the grapple pylon (lets scratch that), and the "places that change" is less of a mechanic and more a design consideration using the other mechanics. I like option A for race track a derelict dreadnaught, but lets improve the idea and instead of just having one ship, its a group of derelict ships, like an ancient battle took place with large ships and we go through and around them."

**Track 01 is the Battle Graveyard**, below. It is generated by `ArtSource/Racing/track_graveyard.py`, with coordinates in [track_01_battle_graveyard.json](track_01_battle_graveyard.json).
- **Mechanics:** nine kept. The grapple pylon is cut. "Places that change" is a design rule that applies the other mechanics, not a mechanic of its own.
- **Options B and C** stay below as reference. Option A (one dreadnought) is superseded by the graveyard.

![Track 01: Battle Graveyard](img/track_01_battle_graveyard.png)

Two fleets died here fighting over an ancient lane-gate. The wrecks:
- **The dreadnought:** a 1.5 km dreadnought broken in two. Its bow drifts, closing **the Break** between the halves from 130 m to 90 m to 50 m across the three laps.
- **The carrier:** its flight deck is open end to end, with two bulkheads to shoot open and a blast door. The door's switch faces the outer line.
- **The battleship:** its guns cover the south straight and wake on lap 2. Its breached reactor pulses across the **keel line** on its north side, and the shadows behind fallen bulkheads are safe.
- **The battleship's engine section:** broken off south of the track, it still fires across the straight.
- **The rest of the fleet:** a cruiser, a burned-out cruiser and two frigates that died rammed into each other.

A salvage rig working the wrecks sweeps the outer corner, and the old minefields were never cleared. The gate itself still works, and it jams for 6 s after each use.

| Route | Clean lap | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| Outer line | 90 s | Salvage-rig arms, the minefield, the south straight under the guns |
| The Break | 87 s | The gap closes every lap; repulsors at the entry |
| Flight deck | 91 s | Bulkheads on lap 1; the door can trap you; no EMP apex |
| Keel line | 96 s | Out of the guns' arcs from lap 2, but across the reactor's pulses |
| Break + keel | 91 s | Both hazards |
| Gate + outer | 76 s | Skips the minefield when the gate is not jammed; the leader can deny it |

## The mechanics

The mechanics the tracks are built from, and the options shown before the decision. All are true-scale top-down maps on the flight plane (SPEC-92 decision 3). Images and coordinates are generated by `ArtSource/Racing/track_layouts.py`; the coordinates RACE-004 needs are in [track_options.json](track_options.json).

**Every mechanic is a general world system.** The owner asked for foundations that work in exploration, not only in races. The race tracks are just the first place they are put together. Each card on the mechanics sheet says what the mechanic does while exploring the galaxy first, then on a track, then what it is built from.

![New mechanics](img/mechanics.png)

## Superseded: Option A, Derelict Run

The single-dreadnought layout, superseded by the Battle Graveyard (its image was retired).

A 1 km dead dreadnought lies across the north-east corner. The lap goes around it, along its flank under its guns, or straight through its hangar. The bulkheads there have to be shot open, and the blast door's switch is on the gun deck.

| Route | Clean lap | What it costs |
|---|---|---|

## Option B: Moon Slingshot

![Option B](img/track_option_b.png)

A figure eight. The east lobe orbits a moon's gravity well:
- **high orbit:** wide, but sunlit and hit by flares;
- **low orbit:** narrow and shadowed, with debris orbiting between the two lines.

The west lobe circles a station whose arms sweep the track, and a pair of lane-gate portals skips the arms. Each portal jams for 6 s after use. The two lobes meet at a level crossing with repulsor mines.

| Route | Clean lap | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| High orbit | 62 s | Flares on the far side |
| Low orbit | 59 s | Narrow, debris, the moon is a wall |
| Portal + high orbit | 50 s | Jammed 6 s after each use: the leader denies it |
| Portal + low orbit | 47 s | The fastest lap, and the most easily denied |

## Option C: Foundry Gauntlet

![Option C](img/track_option_c.png)

An ore foundry has three set pieces:
- a docked freighter that test-fires its engines across the start straight;
- smelter heat vents;
- an ore conveyor carrying rocks across the S-bend.

After the east hairpin the track forks into three lanes. The boost lane runs under a turret platform, and the platform holds the switch for the lane's exit door. The barricade lane is narrow and walled. The safe lane carries the energy canisters. All three merge at an EMP minefield. (The grapple hairpin was removed with the grapple mechanic.)

| Route | Clean lap | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| Safe lane | 71 s | Longest; canisters refill boost |
| Boost lane | 69 s | Four turrets; the exit door can slam |
| Barricade lane | 69 s | Two barricades; one ship blocks it |

## How the lap times are made
- **Flight limits:** a clean line with production flight limits: cap 120 m/s, boost 192 m/s, about 25 m/s² forward, 20 m/s² braking and sideways grip. Carry above the cap bleeds at 8 m/s² (SPEC-91).
- **Grapple and gravity:** the grapple tether adds 40 m/s² of cornering grip within a pylon's reach. The moon adds GM/r².
- **Not modelled:** combat, mines, doors and the moon's speed gain on the dive.
- **The Dart racer** should run about 10% faster on a clean line.

## Building cost (Track 01)

| New systems | Small additions to SPEC-91 | Already exists |
|---|---|---|
| Moving structures (drifting bow, rig arms); mechanisms (bulkheads, blast door and switch); lane-gate portal (ADR) | Reactor pulse with shadows (timed zones plus a shadow test); engine wash; repulsor, seeker and EMP mines; canisters | Station turrets (AI-009), field walls, proximity mines and zones (SPEC-91) |

Every mechanic is built as a general world system in `Game.Simulation.Hazards` (and a mechanisms area), not as racing code (owner, 2026-10-16).
